Legend words match the dots (TASK-306). No All playlists parent; a selects all; status sits beside the mount (TASK-307). Legend labels sit on the row under the rule (TASK-308). Select-all is ^a, quit shows ^q, the playlist scrollbar is hidden, and the track table uses terminal colours (TASK-309). The tree sits on the legend rule; parent guides stay visible on the cursor (TASK-310). Cursor on a crate lights the parent path; a folder still lights every child (TASK-311). Track preview colour is crate membership only; analysis-aware yellow and honest x/y are TASK-303.
MP3 GEOB/GEO write/read is unit-tested for ID3v2.2, v2.3, and v2.4; still not confirmed live in Serato. 36/40 sampled USB MP3s are v2.3; WONSIN Memories and Humble are v2.2

the whole TUI test suite mocks/fakes the rekordbox adapter, so it cannot catch pyo3-level issues like the thread-affinity crash TASK-209 fixed -- that class of bug is only found by running against a real stick. TASK-209's fix is confirmed working on real hardware (user ran a real sync end to end after it); TASK-210, TASK-211, and TASK-212's fixes (refresh-on-resume, synced/total counts, true column alignment, the collapsible "All playlists" node, and the exit-time drop-on-wrong-thread crash) are not yet re-confirmed there -- verified in this environment only via Tree.render_line() output and Pilot tests, both against synthetic fixtures/fakes, never a real PyOneLibrary.

TASK-213's Home screen banner/spinner/error layout was verified via direct widget.render_line() inspection in this environment (region/x-position checks proving each element is independently centered) but not yet seen by the user in a real terminal.

TASK-217's MacVolumesScanner (real deployment target: /Volumes on macOS) and WindowsMountScanner are both verified only against monkeypatched directory trees in this environment -- neither has run on real macOS or Windows hardware. TASK-217 also removed the WSL-specific /mnt auto-scan (LinuxMntScanner) since real deployment is Windows/Linux/macOS, not WSL; this project's own dev/test sandbox now reaches its /mnt/usb test stick via the USBVERSAL_MOUNT env var override instead.
